plan.title: bug(hooks): commit file-set snapshot uses the payload root, so a bound worktree still refuses a subagent's commit

narratives.Description: The #5656 commit-shape check read every word after the git commit options that does not start with - as a file name, so a message-only commit that ends in 2>&1 | tail -N was refused as if it changed the file set after the pre-tool index snapshot; the issue blamed the index root, but that refusal is printed before any index read and the read already uses the named worktree. This story teaches the check that a pipe ends the commit, that a redirection and its target are not arguments, and that short-option clusters follow git, keeps the #6187 heredoc chunking with chunk boundaries that are not &&, and makes the refusal name the word that tripped it. Real -a, --all, --include and file-name commits stay refused, and the story binding and index root are not changed.
narratives.Overview:
1. Operators. In `tokenizeShellCommand`, `&&`, `||` and `|&` are recognized before a lone `|`, and a `|` right after `>` is part of that redirect (`>|`). An unquoted lone `|` or `|&` ends the segment as a separator that is not `&&`, so the words after it are not commit arguments and a `cd` joined to the commit by a pipe stays unresolvable.
2. Redirections. Escape processing comes first, and `<` and `>` join the unquoted escapable set, so `\>path` is one literal word. A word that starts with `<(` or `>(` is an argument. An unquoted, unescaped redirection is optional digits or one `&`, then `<` or `>`; it is not an argument, and neither is its target: the attached rest of the word, or the next word when the operator stands alone. Any other prefix, such as `*`, makes the word an argument. Words after a redirection are still read.
3. Short-option clusters follow git. Letters are read in order. `a` or `i` marks the commit as index-changing while it is still an option letter. The first of `m`, `F`, `c`, `C` or `t` takes the rest of the cluster as its value, or the next word when it is the last letter. `u` and `S` take the rest of the cluster and never the next word.
4. Heredoc. `resolveCommitTarget`, `commandHasGitCommitIndexMutatingForm` and `commandHasGitCommitSubcommand` read the chunks of `shellCommandChunksWithoutQuotedHereDocBodies`. Each chunk is tokenized on its own, with no join before `tokenizeShellCommand`. The segments of all chunks then form one list in chunk order, and the last segment of each chunk ends with a separator that is not `&&`, so `resolveOneCommit` sees every earlier `cd` and a `cd` in an earlier chunk makes the target unresolvable. This story carries that wiring unless #6481 has merged it in that shape. An unquoted body stays visible.
5. Message. The #5656 index-snapshot refusal names the first word that made the commit index-changing.
6. Unchanged. `-a`, `--all`, `-i`, `--include`, `-am` and any real trailing file name, also after `--` or after a redirection, are refused. A quoted operator, a lone `&` and a `#` word are ordinary words and are refused as today. The staged index is read on the target root as today. `resolveWorktreeStoryBinding` and `evaluateProspectiveScopeCover` are not changed.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Given a bound linked worktree with a staged index, when a background subagent runs `git -C <wt> commit -m msg 2>&1 | tail -3` or `cd <wt> && git commit -F <file> 2>&1 | tail -3`, then the commit-shape check does not refuse and the staged index is read on that worktree.
- Given `git commit -qm msg`, or `git commit -F - <<'EOF'` with a message body, then the commit is not index-changing.
- Given `-a`, `-am msg`, `-qam msg`, or a trailing file name after the message, after `--`, or after a redirection (`2>&1 src/a.ts`), then the commit is refused.
- Given `-tm src/a.ts`, `-um src/a.ts` or `-Sm src/a.ts`, then the commit is refused.
- Given `\>src/a.ts`, `*>src/a.ts`, `*> src/a.ts`, `<(printf src/a.ts)`, `'|'` or `'>x'` after the message, then the commit is refused.
- Given `true || cd /x && git commit -m msg` or `cd /x | git commit -m msg`, then the target is unresolvable as today.
- Given `cd <wt> <<EOF`, an unquoted body, the `EOF` line, and `git commit -m msg` on the next line, then the target is unresolvable as today.
- Given `cd <wt> <<EOF && git commit -m msg` with an unquoted body after that line, then the target is `<wt>`.
- Given a quoted-delimiter heredoc whose body holds the line `git commit -a`, or a quoted string argument that holds it, then the command is not read as a commit.
- Given an unquoted-delimiter heredoc whose body holds the line `git commit -a`, then the commit is refused as today.
- Given an unquoted heredoc body with an open quote followed, after the delimiter, by `git commit -a`, then the commit is refused.
- The index-snapshot refusal names the word that tripped it.
narratives.Constraint:
- Reading the index from another root (the issue's guess): the refusal is printed before any index read, and that read already uses the named worktree (comment 6940423436, Road not taken).
- Parsing a lone `&`, `#` comments, PowerShell `*>` or nested shells: not in the logged forms; this is not a general shell interpreter (comment 6940423436, finding 5; comment 6940667523, finding 1).
- Waiting for #6481 before carrying the heredoc wiring (comment 6940423436, finding 4).
- Joining a chunk that starts with `&&` to the `cd` of an earlier chunk (comment 6940667523, finding 2 disposition): a line that starts with `&&` after a heredoc delimiter is a shell syntax error, so that commit never runs. See `A1`.
narratives.UserStory: As a story worker committing in a bound linked worktree, I want a message-only git commit with a trailing 2>&1 | tail to be admitted while a real -a or file-name commit is still refused, so that I can commit without rewriting the command and can see which word a refusal is about.
narratives.ImplementationPlan:
1. packages/core/src/hooks/commit-target.ts tokenizeShellCommand: recognize &&, || and |& before a lone |; a | right after > stays in the redirect word; an unquoted lone | or |& ends the segment with a separator that is not &&. Add < and > to the unquoted escapable set and mark a word as a redirection when its unescaped, unquoted start is optional digits or one & then < or >, except <( and >(.
2. packages/core/src/hooks/commit-target.ts commitArgsMutateIndex: skip redirection words and, when the operator stands alone, the next word; read short clusters in git order (a/i mark; m, F, c, C, t take rest or next word; u, S take only the rest); return the first tripping word, and export a helper that gives that word for the command.
3. packages/core/src/hooks/commit-target.ts commandSegments: keep the #6481 per-chunk tokenize and make each chunk's last segment end with a non-&& boundary.
4. packages/core/src/hooks/dispatcher.ts: the #5656 refusal sentence names the tripping word from that helper.
5. Tests in packages/core/src/hooks/commit-target.test.ts and packages/core/src/hooks/dispatcher-commit-heredoc.test.ts for every Acceptance Criterion, and changelog.d/6471-commit-shape-pipes-and-redirects.md.

A worker in a bound worktree cannot commit: the hook refuses with the message that the commit "changes the file set after the pre-tool index snapshot". The issue guessed that the hook reads the wrong checkout's index. The session logs show a simpler cause. Every refused commit ended with `2>&1 | tail -N`. The same check also reads text inside a heredoc as commands, so a note that only mentions a commit is refused. The recommended fix teaches the argument scan that a pipe ends the command and that a redirection is not a file name, and reuses the heredoc fix that #6187 already has in review. - P1 — Given a linked worktree bound to its story with a staged index, when a background subagent commits there with only a message, then the index snapshot is taken from that worktree and the commit is admitted.

The refusal comes from one command-text check: after the commit's options, every word that does not start with `-` is treated as a file name. `2>&1`, a pipe, and `tail` are such words, so a message-only commit written with a log suffix looks like it changes the file set. The same commit with that suffix removed does not trip the check. The staged index that runs afterward is already taken in the checkout named by `git -C` or by `cd … &&`, which is the worktree when the command names it.

The pipe rule, the redirect rule, and the heredoc-chunk reuse are the right mechanism. The short-option rule, as written, is not: it lets a real pathspec commit through.

Question 1. That snapshot sentence has one producer, and it runs before the index read. For the logged `2>&1 | tail` forms, the pipe and the redirect are the whole cause. The pain does not need a second index root.

Question 2. A quoted `'|'` or `'>x'`, a process substitution kept as an argument, and a real `>|` redirect match the shell and still refuse a path the shell actually passes to git. Two wordings open a hole: a short cluster whose first argument-taking letter is not `m`, `F`, `c`, or `C`, and an escaped `\>path` if `<` and `>` are recognized before escape processing. Splitting `||` into two pipes sends the scope check at a different checkout than the one the shell commits in.

Question 3. This story carries the heredoc wiring. The helper is already in the tree and neither commit detector calls it, so waiting leaves the heredoc pain open. Naming the word that tripped the check is worth the change to the existing denial sentence.

Otherwise a letter `a` or `i` anywhere in the cluster refuses (262), and any other dash-word is skipped (263–265), so the next word hits 267 and is refused. `-t`, `-u`, and `-S` are absent from `COMMIT_VALUE_OPTIONS`. Today `git commit -tm src/a.ts` is refused at 267.

Failure mode: C4 reads letters in order and lets the first of `m`, `F`, `c`, `C` take the rest of the cluster or the next word. On `-tm src/a.ts` that reads `m` as the message and admits the commit. Git's own short-option rule gives the rest of the cluster to the first short that takes an argument, so `-t` takes `m` as the template file and `src/a.ts` is a pathspec. The same split happens for an attached optional argument: `-um src/a.ts` and `-Sm src/a.ts` are pathspec commits, and C4 reads them as message-only. This is a regression. The current scanner refuses all three. P2 stops holding for a trailing pathspec hidden behind a message letter.

Disposition: C4 cannot bind as written. The cluster rule that can bind is git's: the first argument-taking short consumes the rest of the cluster. `t` takes a required argument, with `m`, `F`, `c`, and `C`. `u` and `S` take an attached optional argument and do not take the next word. `a` or `i` marks the commit only while that letter is still an option, which keeps `-am` refused and keeps `-qm msg` message-only.

Evidence: `packages/core/src/hooks/commit-target.ts` 96–99 ends a segment only when `&` or `|` is doubled, so `||` is one separator. 368–373 treats `segments[cdIndex - 1].next === "||"` as unresolvable, because `true || cd /x && git commit` skips the `cd` and commits in the inherited cwd. Failure mode: C1 says an unquoted `|` ends the command, and names `|&`, without saying what happens to a second `|`. A character scan that splits every `|` turns `||` into two pipes. The `cd` skip then stops firing, and `true || cd /wrong && git commit -m msg` is judged at `/wrong` while the shell commits in the inherited checkout. Disposition: C1 can bind with the match order stated. `&&` and `||` stay the doubled operators they are now, recognized before a lone `|`. `|&` is one operator, recognized before a lone `|`. A `|` immediately after `>` is part of the redirect, not a pipe. A lone `|` is a separator other than `&&`, so a `cd` joined to the commit by a pipe stays unresolvable.

### 3. `sharpens-framing` — A redirect is an unescaped operator, and `<(` stays a pathspec

Escape processing happens first, and `<` and `>` join the unquoted escapable set so `\>path` remains one word and still counts as a pathspec. A word that starts with `<(` or `>(` is an argument. Only then is an unquoted, unescaped redirect removed, including an attached target, or the next word when the target is separate. A later `-a` or file name still counts.

Skipping the wiring leaves a quoted heredoc body as its own segments, and a note that only mentions a commit is still refused.

Disposition: C3 can bind as a call, on each chunk, from all three detectors, with no join before `tokenizeShellCommand`. The production pair is the two calls in `decideProspectiveGitCommitScopeCover`; the test-only detector stays on the same chunks. This story carries that wiring. The denial text at `packages/core/src/hooks/dispatcher.ts` 5225–5227 names `-a`, `--all`, `-am`, `--include`, and pathspecs. A refusal caused by `|` or `2>&1` reads as an index-root failure. The prefix is optional file-descriptor digits or one leading `&`, then `<` or `>`. ## Bound remedy
1. Operators. In `tokenizeShellCommand`, `&&`, `||` and `|&` are recognized before a lone `|`, and a `|` right after `>` is part of that redirect (`>|`). An unquoted lone `|` or `|&` ends the segment as a separator that is not `&&`, so the words after it are not commit arguments and a `cd` joined to the commit by a pipe stays unresolvable.
2. Redirections. Escape processing comes first, and `<` and `>` join the unquoted escapable set, so `\>path` is one literal word. A word that starts with `<(` or `>(` is an argument. An unquoted, unescaped redirection is optional digits or one `&`, then `<` or `>`; it is not an argument, and neither is its target: the attached rest of the word, or the next word when the operator stands alone. Any other prefix, such as `*`, makes the word an argument. Words after a redirection are still read.
3. Short-option clusters follow git. Letters are read in order. `a` or `i` marks the commit as index-changing while it is still an option letter. The first of `m`, `F`, `c`, `C` or `t` takes the rest of the cluster as its value, or the next word when it is the last letter. `u` and `S` take the rest of the cluster and never the next word.

## Problem

After #6379, a worktree bound by `swarm:pre-dispatch` begin lets a worker commit with no `DEFT_ACTIVE_SCOPE`, but only when the worker's host session has that worktree as its own root. A background subagent running inside a parent session rooted at the primary checkout is still refused on every commit form, with the #5656 message that the commit "changes the file set after the pre-tool index snapshot".

Reported by a worker, not re-read in source: the pre-tool index snapshot appears to come from the payload root (the primary checkout, nothing staged), while the commit aimed at the worktree commits that worktree's index (one staged file), so the file set looks changed. Hook messages in the same run name `payloadRoot=C:\Repos\deft\directive`.

The same check also refuses a shell command whose text only quotes commit flags inside a heredoc body (seen in the parent session while filing this issue).

## Evidence (2026-11-16, runtime 0.129.11)

- #6337, run as its own host session with the worktree as its folder and bound with pre-dispatch begin: the commit was admitted (2cd4571b3, PR #6470).
- #6366, run as a background subagent of a parent rooted at the primary checkout and bound the same way (attempt att-1387afff34d3caa4): five commit forms were refused, including a dry-run with only a message, both with the worktree named on the command and after changing into it, with only the brief staged.
- The same worker's write into the worktree's gitignored `.deft-scratch/` was refused because the fence base is origin/master, where the new brief is not active yet.

- Given the same commit that adds a real trailing pathspec or the all-files flag, then it is still refused.
- Given a shell command that only quotes commit flags inside a heredoc or string, then the commit-shape check does not treat it as a commit.
